title: Anion gap is a predictor of elevated serum lactate in patients diagnosed with sepsis without shock in the emergency department
core_idea: Evaluate whether higher anion gap values predict elevated serum lactate (specifically >2 mmol/l and >4 mmol/l) and determine optimal anion gap cut-off points in patients with sepsis without shock presenting to the emergency department, using retrospective clinical and laboratory data and ROC analysis.
tldr: Retrospective ED study to assess if anion gap predicts elevated lactate levels in non-shock sepsis and to identify optimal AG cut-offs for lactate >2 and >4 mmol/l.
